memories.memory: I bring home about $2,300 a month from repair and installation work, but the amount changes when there are fewer construction jobs.
In February 2024, I borrowed roughly $4,800 from my older brother to replace the welding machine in my workshop, and I am repaying him in $200 monthly installments.
I keep around $9,000 in savings as an emergency fund, although I was tempted to use most of it last year to buy a second-hand delivery van.
When a former coworker opened a small metalworking business, I invested $3,500 in it without taking out a formal loan because I believed the workshop would become profitable.
I am still paying off about $6,700 on a used van, with a monthly payment of approximately $290 due near the end of each month.
A customer delayed paying my $1,150 invoice for nearly three months, which forced me to postpone buying new tools and take extra weekend jobs.
I set aside a small cash envelope from every completed job to cover taxes and insurance, and by the end of last year it had reached about $2,400.
